Finding:
↑ Transplant-related mortality
Transplant-related mortality was 9%, 23%, and 53% for high, intermediate and low diversity groups, respectively (p = 0.03).
Patients with low diversity (inverse Simpson < 2) were 7.5 times more likely to experience transplant-related mortality within the follow-up when compared to those with higher microbial diversity (HR 7.54; 95% CI 2.12–47.88; p = 0.001; adjusted hazard ratio, 5.25; 95% CI 1.36–35.07; p = 0.014).

↑ Transplantation-related Mortality
When compared to patients in the high diversity group, patients in the low-diversity group had higher estimated 2-year transplanted related mortality (20.0% vs. 4.7%; p = 0.04).
After adjusting for pretransplant comorbidity, disease status at the time of allo-HSCT and previous chemotherapy, low intestinal diversity was an independent predictor of transplant-related mortality (HR 4.95; 95% CI 1.03–23.76; p = 0.046).

↓ Transplantation-related Mortality
The Shannon diversity index at the time of engraftment was significantly associated with transplantation-related mortality (coefficient = −1.44; p = 0.02)

↓ GvHD-related mortality
Increased intestinal diversity was associated with reduced GvHD-related mortality (p = 0.005).

↑ aGvHD
Decreased intestinal diversity at D + 10 was associated with increased risk of early onset aGvHD (OR 7.833; 95% CI 2.141–28.658; p = 0.038).

↑ GvHD-related mortality
GvHD-related mortality was higher in patients with low diversity (p = 0.018).
